title: Why Your Brain Can't Forget on Command #Shorts
description:
Trying to stop thinking about something only makes it louder in your mind. Here is why mental suppression backfires and how to actually break the loop. Like and subscribe for daily psychology facts!
#psychology #mindtricks #brainfacts #humanbehavior
script: Your brain is physically incapable of forgetting on command. In 1987, Harvard psychologist Daniel Wegner told people not to think about a white bear. Every time they did, they had to ring a bell. Participants rang it once every minute. Trying to suppress a thought actually makes you think about it twice as much, because your brain constantly checks for it. That is why lying in bed telling yourself not to remember an embarrassing moment makes it loop on repeat. To break the loop today, use focused distraction: count backward from one hundred by sevens. By trying not to think about it, you just trapped it in your mind. Be honest: what is the one forbidden thought you are trying to suppress right now? Follow for one psychology fact every day.
